newsitem.title: FRANCE: Syrian officials in Paris to discuss peace process.
newsitem.headline: Syrian officials in Paris to discuss peace process.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara will visit Paris on Thursday for talks on the stalled Middle East peace process, France said on Wednesday.
The Foreign Ministry said the two Syrian officials would meet French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette over lunch, followed by a news briefing.
A ministry spokesman said the meeting would enable de Charette to get the Syrian point of view before a Middle East tour next week starting with Israel.
"Our Israeli friends will be quite happy to know the Syrian point of view," spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
De Charette plans to visit Israel, Lebanon and Syria from March 4-6.
Israel last week lodged an official complaint after Paris disclosed that de Charette would spend just 24 hours in the Jewish state.
Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor said on Monday that Paris had originally promised "a full state visit of two or three days".
Damascus said earlier this week that its officials planned to tour European capitals to explain Syria's position on its stalled peace talks with Israel.
Syria is angry over Israel's refusal to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Since hardliner Benjamin Netanyahu's election last year as prime minister, Arab countries have been warning Israel not to deviate from the concept of trading land for peace, as endorsed by Israel's previous Labour government.
